$comment: Oracle — investment-cost and market-stress cases. MIXED PROVENANCE: the shock magnitudes are a repo product decision and the long-horizon fee-drag case is repo-designed; only the fee-drag PRINCIPLE and the past-performance rule are taken from the cited SEC bulletins. Each case names its own source key. An annual investment cost is a flat mean-shift of cost/12 percentage points on each month's blended return; the named stresses compose additively on that same shift; the longevity stress extends the horizon but never past age 105. Expected values are derived independently from the cited sources, never from production code.

sec-fees-bulletin.name: SEC Investor.gov — Investor Bulletin: How fees and expenses affect your investment portfolio
sec-fees-bulletin.publication: updated investor bulletin (no dated revision on the page)
sec-fees-bulletin.identifier: PRINCIPLE ONLY, not a reproduced worked example: an ongoing annual fee reduces the portfolio's return by that fee each year; the shortfall compounds, so a small annual fee costs a large share of the ending balance over a long horizon. The bulletin's own illustration uses different parameters; the long-horizon case below is repo-designed (see `repo-designed-fee-drag`).

repo-designed-fee-drag.name: Repo-designed long-horizon fee-drag illustration
repo-designed-fee-drag.publication: repo-designed, 2026-08-10 (parameters chosen here, NOT taken from any publication)
repo-designed-fee-drag.identifier: $100,000 compounded for 360 months at a 0.85% monthly blended return, with and without a 0.50% annual investment cost. Parameters are chosen to match the portfolio and month used by the two exact cases above so the three cases compose; the arithmetic is derived independently in this fixture and only the DIRECTION and compounding principle come from the SEC bulletin.

sec-performance-claims.name: SEC Investor.gov — Investor Bulletin: Performance claims
sec-performance-claims.identifier: Past performance is not indicative of future results; a past return may not be presented as a forecast

stress-magnitudes.name: Repo product decision — approved market-stress magnitudes
stress-magnitudes.identifier: Higher fees +0.50 pp; lower returns stocks -2 pp / bonds and cash -1 pp; higher inflation +2 pp; longer life +5 years capped at age 105

cases.description: A 0.50% annual investment cost applied to a 60/30/10 portfolio in a month returning 1.20% on stocks, 0.40% on bonds, and 0.10% on cash.
derivation: Annual cost 0.50 percent spread evenly = 0.50/12 = 0.0416666666666667 percent per month.

cases.description: Same portfolio and month, with the fee and return shocks applied together: 0.50% extra annual cost AND the per-sleeve return reduction (stocks -2 pp, bonds and cash -1 pp).
derivation: Blended annual return reduction = 0.60*2 + 0.30*1 + 0.10*1 = 1.2 + 0.3 + 0.1 = 1.6 pp per year; per month = 1.6/12 = 0.13333333333333333 percent.
Composition is additive: applying the fee shock and the return shock together equals the sum of the two individual shifts.

cases.description: Repo-designed fee-drag illustration (source `repo-designed-fee-drag`, NOT the SEC bulletin's own worked example): $100,000 held for 30 years at a 0.85%/month gross blended return, with and without a 0.50% annual investment cost. Only the compounding principle and the direction come from the SEC bulletin.
derivation: Shortfall = 2105352.97 - 1814330.73 = 291022.24 dollars, i.e. the ongoing 0.50 percent fee costs about 13.8 percent of the ending balance over 30 years.
Direction: a fee can only lower the ending balance, never raise it.

cases.description: The longer-life stress extends the horizon by five years, but never past the longest-lived member's age-105 year.

derivation: Extended = 2085; age-105 year = 2075; min = 2075, but the stress must never SHORTEN a horizon, so max(2080, 2075) = 2080.
